designGate.prompt: Before writing code, sketch the classes you intend and how you will store events. Name the data structure backing lookups by type.

parts.title: Append and read back

hints.text: What is the minimum state an EventLog needs to answer size() and all()?
A vector of records is enough for part 1. Think about what a record is: a type and a payload.
Store a vector of pair<string, string>. append() pushes, all() returns a copy in insertion order.

probes: What is the complexity of append here?
If I asked for events of one type, would your current storage help you?

parts.title: Query by type

hints.text: A linear scan passes these tests. Is that the answer you would give in an interview?
Consider maintaining an index from event type to the events of that type, updated on append.
Keep an unordered_map from event_type to a vector. append() writes to both the main log and the index.

probes: What did that cost you on append?
Your index duplicates the events. What happens if one of them is removed?

parts.title: Bounded capacity

hints.text: Eviction removes an event from the main log. Does anything else still point at it?
Every structure holding a reference to an event must be updated when that event is evicted. That is the cost of the index you added in part 2.
Switch the log to a deque. On eviction, pop_front and remove the same event from its type bucket, erasing the bucket when it empties.

probes: Did your part-2 index survive this change, or did you have to rework it?
What would break if two events of the same type were evicted out of order?

criteria: deque for O(1) eviction from the front
edge cases considered before being told
stated the tradeoff when adding the index
